idea: An AI study planner app for JEE aspirants that adjusts the timetable after every mock test

strategist.problem: A Class 11 or 12 JEE aspirant in India finishes a mock test on a Sunday evening, sees the score and topic-wise errors, and has no idea how to rewrite next week's timetable around them — so the plan they made on Monday collapses by Wednesday and the same weak chapters stay unprepared until the next test.
strategist.target_customer: Parents of Class 11 and 12 JEE aspirants in India, household income roughly ₹5-25 lakh per year, who already pay for coaching and buy anything that visibly disciplines their child's study hours — they subscribe monthly because they can see the regenerated timetable in their child's app each week.
strategist.mission: Give every JEE aspirant a timetable that rewrites itself from their latest mock test so weak chapters get the hours they actually need.

competitors.name: Allen, Aakash and FIITJEE in-house study planners and DPP schedules
competitors.differentiator: Their plans are fixed batch-wide and updated by a teacher weeks apart; ours regenerates per student within minutes of every mock test at a fraction of a coaching fee.

competitors.name: Self-made timetables in Google Sheets or a paper diary
competitors.differentiator: A static sheet cannot re-allocate hours from a test score; we do that automatically, which is the part students abandon first.

competitors.name: Generic AI chat assistants like ChatGPT asked to 'make a study plan'
competitors.differentiator: A chat reply is one-off text with no saved state, no test-score input and no next-week diff — we persist the plan and update it after each test.

scope_cuts: Skipping a built-in mock test engine or question bank — we ingest scores the student already gets from their coaching's tests, which keeps us out of content licensing and lets us ship in 3-4 weeks.

Skipping a separate parent dashboard or WhatsApp parent alerts in v1 — the parent pays for the visible weekly timetable in the student's app; a second portal doubles build surface for a founder working 15 hours a week.
Skipping Android/iOS native apps and a desktop client at launch — one mobile-web app the student opens after every test is enough to prove the re-planning loop before any platform work.

mvp_features: 1. Mock-test score intake + auto-regenerated weekly timetable: student enters topic-wise scores, the app re-allocates hours to weak chapters and shows the next-week plan diff (the moment the parent pays)
2. Saved plan state with week-over-week history so the timetable persists instead of being a one-off chat reply
3. Razorpay Subscription checkout (UPI e-mandate auto-debit) gating week 2+ regeneration, with the regenerated timetable emailed to the parent via Resend

first_10_steps: Run `npx create-next-app@latest jee-replan --ts --tailwind --app` and push it to a new GitHub repo
Create a Supabase project and run SQL for `students`, `mock_tests`, `test_topic_scores`, `weekly_plans` tables with row-level security on user_id
Sign up for the GitHub Student Developer Pack and enable GitHub Copilot Student, then verify a college email on BharatCode for the free API key
Build the score-intake screen: a form for test name, date, total score, and per-topic marks for Physics/Chemistry/Maths chapters
Write the regeneration prompt in Claude and call BharatCode's Qwen endpoint from a Next.js route handler to return a JSON weekly timetable with hours per chapter
Render the regenerated timetable as a 7-day grid with a 'changed from last week' diff highlighting hours added to weak chapters
Deploy to Netlify free tier with `netlify deploy` and connect the `.in` domain from Cloudflare Registrar

Activate Razorpay Subscriptions: create a recurring ₹299 plan with UPI e-mandate auto-debit, and gate week 2+ regeneration behind an active `subscription_status = 'active'` check (fall back to a manually re-sent Razorpay payment link each month if e-mandate fails, blocking regeneration when no active subscription exists)
Wire Resend to email the regenerated timetable to the parent's address each Sunday after a test is submitted
Post the live link in 5 class/hostel WhatsApp groups and DM 10 batchmates' parents with a 1-week free trial of the regenerated timetable

key_assumptions: Willingness to pay ₹299/month rests on the assumption that parents already pay ₹1,000-3,000/month for coaching and will pay roughly 10% of that for a visible weekly timetable in their child's app.

Delivery cost of ₹12/customer/month is an assumption: BharatCode Qwen regeneration tokens are free on the student tier, plus Resend free-tier emails and Razorpay 2% + GST on ₹299 (~₹7); it rises if regeneration volume exceeds free tiers.
Blended avg revenue of ₹299 assumes ~1 in 6 buyers picks the ₹799 term pass instead of ₹299 monthly.
Free trials and the free first week reduce revenue and are not counted in burn or marketing.

channels.name: Class & hostel WhatsApp groups (student-to-parent loop)
channels.tactic: Join 10 JEE Class 11/12 WhatsApp groups (own coaching batch, seniors/juniors, hostel floor, 2 parent-teacher groups). Post 1 message per group per week: free-week app link + one sample regenerated timetable screenshot. Then DM the 2 most engaged parents in each group personally with the cold message. Volume: 10 group posts + 20 parent DMs per week = 40 group posts + 80 parent DMs per month.

channels.name: Coaching parent WhatsApp communities + YouTube Shorts (parent-facing)
channels.tactic: Get added to 5 JEE coaching parent WhatsApp groups (ask your own coaching's parent coordinator, or a batchmate's parent to introduce you). Post 1 message per group per week with the free-week app link. In parallel, post 1 YouTube Short/day (30/month, 20-sec screen recording: mock score in, timetable regenerated, weak-chapter diff) titled in Hinglish for parents, and reply to every comment with the free-week link. Rs 0 spend on CapCut free + phone screen record.

first_10_customers: Day 1-3: Send the cold message to 20 parents already in your coaching's parent WhatsApp group and your own relatives/neighbours with a Class 11/12 child — give them the free-week app link and ask them to have their child enter one real mock score.

Day 4-7: In your own JEE batch WhatsApp group, post 1 message: 'enter your last mock score in this app, it rewrites your week's timetable free for 7 days' — ask each batchmate to forward the link to their parent.

Day 8-14: Get added to 5 coaching parent WhatsApp groups (via your coaching's parent coordinator or a batchmate's parent) and post 1 message per group per week with the free-week link; DM the 2 parents who react or reply in each group.
Day 15-21: Call the 6 parents who used the free week (voice note or 2-min call): ask what stopped them subscribing, fix that one thing, then send a Razorpay payment link at Rs 299.

Day 22-30: Ask every paying parent to forward the Razorpay link to 1 parent in their coaching's parent group; give the referrer's child an extra regenerated timetable week (no cash discount). Target: 5 paying by Day 30.
growth.cold_message: Namaste, I'm a Class 12 student building a planner that rewrites your child's weekly timetable from their latest mock test score — weak chapters automatically get more hours. Here's a free-week link: have your child enter one real mock score and the app regenerates the full week itself, no payment needed. If it looks useful, it's Rs 299/month and the new timetable lands in your inbox every week.

objections.objection: Coaching already gives my child a study plan, why pay Rs 299 more?
objections.response: Coaching plans are batch-wide and updated weeks apart. Ours regenerates within minutes of every mock test, per your child's own topic-wise errors. Take the free-week link, have them enter one real score, and compare the regenerated timetable before paying anything.

objections.objection: Rs 299/month is just another subscription my child won't use.
objections.response: You see the regenerated timetable in your inbox every week, so you'll know it's being used. Cancel any month — no lock-in. Start with the free first week, pay only after you've seen 1 real regenerated timetable.

critic.verdict: The plan stays faithful to the AI study planner for JEE aspirants with mock-test-driven timetable regeneration, and it fits a bootstrapped student founder with a savings-sized budget, free tiers and a campus-first WhatsApp launch. Pricing at ₹299/month is realistic for Indian parents already paying coaching fees, and the 3-4 week ship timeline with a 6-week first-paying-customer goal is achievable at 15 hours/week. The main weaknesses are in the growth playbook's volume assumptions and a couple of unverified tool choices, but nothing breaks the hard rules.
critic.biggest_risk: Conversion from free-week trials to paid parents stalls because the parent never actually sees their child use the app, so the weekly emailed timetable never lands or is ignored — killing the one value signal the ₹299 subscription rests on.
